See the Liverpool media team has done his job judging by the comments. "Massive ego", "terrible attitude", etc. It's genuinely always amazed me how football fans seem to absolutely oblivious to how Communications Departments work at football Clubs and how much their perceptions are literally relying on them.

Clubs worked out a long time ago that there's two ways to shape a story - the first is by giving reporters the information that you want reported in a quid pro quo, they print what they almost certainly know to be bollocks but they also know that down the line they'll be the first to get a decent story and will be seen as "one of the good guys".
Good example - Paul Joyce broke a story that Sterling will be earning £200,000 a week at City and is believed because "he's reliable on Liverpool". Anybody who knows even the slightest bit about City will be able to tell that that is absolutely bollocks because our contracts are heavily structured since 2012 and not even Sergio Aguero earns £200k basic. The smarter ones might also be asking "hold on, how does this Liverpool based journalist know absolutely anything about the contract negotiations between Sterling and Man City?". The answer is that he doesn't but it's extremely important to Liverpool that they shape any outgoing superstar as a moneygrabber when it allows them to.

Coincidentally, this is straight out of the Arsenal playbook and how they've operated for years. They understand that if they shape the message correctly then the fans will actually be thanking the Club for selling one of their best players rather than asking questions about it. It's very much easier to get away with it when somebody is going to City for three reasons; firstly a large number of the social media louder fans of Arsenal and Liverpool despise City because we've taken their birthright. Secondly, City have had a message straight from the top that we don't do our business in public and we will not be making any comment on any situation. Thirdly, because City have money so the "money grabber" narrative is just so damn easy. Hell, Arsenal were so entrenched in this that their PR department actually tried to spin RvP to United as a money grabbing move. Have to admire the balls on them for that.

Let's just give a timeline here, so those who haven't followed the situation or might not know actually understand what happened:

  • The first real discontent heard was when Brendan Rodgers spoke in a press conference about how they've made Sterling "an incredible offer" and how he thinks he has been badly advised.

This started the wheels turning - Liverpool knew on the day he spoke those words that Sterling was gone and the battle for hearts and minds started. Immediately ex-Liverpool players started coincidentally getting media interviews and were slating Sterling as a mercenary. Sterling was refused any right of reply by the Club and had to basically sit back and watch the world insult him because Liverpool said he did, a Club which he had already probably decided to leave.

  • Sterling, sick of the comments in the press, bypasses Liverpool's media block on him and arranges an interview with the BBC to present his side of the story. During this time he says that it isn't about money but because he wants to win things.

The Liverpool based press immediately spin this not as a player giving out his wishes straight from the horses mouth, but instead focus on the absolute gall that he has to bypass Liverpool's censorship of him, calling him unprofessional and how he has a bad attitude for not sitting back and letting himself be buried by unfair criticism so FSG can come out of this looking good. More ex-players coincidentally turn up to insult Sterling through the press.

  • His agent gives an interview where he again attempts to put across Sterling's side and claim that it's not about money at all and he wouldn't sign for Liverpool for £900k a week as the money is irrelevant.

The press immediately focuses on how the agent is a prick for giving the interview defending his client who was getting slaughtered by all sides unfairly. He again tried to tell people that it isn't about money but instead about trophies and the Liverpool press corps absolutely ate him up. Again nobody seemed to mention that Sterling consistently said "I don't care about the money, I want to win things".

  • Sterling goes back to his pre-season training on the allotted day. On this day he has a 30 minute meeting with Brendan Rodgers where the conclusion is reached that it probably isn't the best idea to have him on the pre-season tour to distract the training sessions and allow Rodgers to get them/new players mentally focused. Rodgers already knows that he's gone and makes no attempt to convince him to stay. Sterling already knows he's gone and makes no attempts to ask to stay.

Hilariously (and this is where I expected most fans to wake up to this but alas they didn't), somebody at Liverpool immediately leaks this meeting to the press. In it they suggest that Sterling had single handedly refused to go on a pre-season tour with Liverpool.

I've said previously that I'm fucking angry at the way that Liverpool have handled this situation and the incident above is the actual root of that. The rest of this was football bollocks that is to be expected, there was absolutely NO reason to leak that meeting suggesting that he solely took that decision (which he absolutely didn't and contractually if he did then Liverpool could have sued him for and stopped his bog move). It changed the narrative into one of him being a money grabber which fans were irritated at, to him being Osama bin Sterling which people were genuinely fucking angry at.

So then people start sending death threats and racist abuse to Sterling. They show up at his house and damage his property. They write messages telling him to hug his daughter because they're going to murder her. His phone number was leaked and people spent the entire night ringing him, telling him they were going to burn his house down with him and his family inside of it.

  • The next day Sterling told Liverpool that he wouldn't be coming into training because he was ill. Well he didn't, he told them that he was petrified for his life and wanted to sort out some arrangements for security and wouldn't leave his house until he did. Liverpool told the unofficially press that he was faking it and said he had "diarrhoea". I have to say that if I was running the City communications department on that day then I would have cashed in every single favour in the world and blew Liverpool out of the water for this, but it would both cause hold ups in the deal and would be against company policy.

  • Sterling, after two days to get things together, returned to training. This was roundly greeted with more derision because showing up for training is proof that you weren't ill or something apparently.

The entire way that Liverpool has handled this has legitimately made me angry and feel that it should be illegal or something. At one point, the first day when he said he wasn't going in, you got the feeling that people in the press were willing him to suicide or hoping he'd get caught by one of those death threats. It was disgusting.

This is over and above football rivalries and if City did something like this I'd be ashamed to call myself a Blue. Arsenal paint their outgoings as moneygrabbers and that's fine because it's part of the game and they are only hurting feelings. Liverpool purposefully and professionally whipped up and maintained a frenzy against Sterling with stories planted every single day, that resulted in their idiot fans going too far. If they then would have pulled back, I'd put it down to them maybe not realising how the anger was manifesting and wouldn't really have a problem with it. People make mistakes. But they didn't. They saw he was getting racial abuse and people saying they were going to murder his daughter, and tried to ramp it up again by suggesting he was faking illness to create more anger.

I don't know whose decision this media campaign was but cannot imagine that this came from Sue Black. Either somebody there was completely oblivious and fucked up badly or they weren't and they need to be immediately sacked.

Please check out this NVIDIA presentation on Vulkan if you haven't already. Of particular interest (perhaps also to your readers) are the bits about Vulkan and OpenGL living merrily together and how that all works.

For instance:

  • Vulkan will work anywhere OpenGL works

  • Vulkan and OpenGL share a driver and share resources

  • devs can incrementally add Vulkan support

  • If devs use some OpenGL and some Vulkan, they won't interfere with each other or slow each other down.

  • Vulkan is at heart engineered to facilitate an easy transition and sharing the driver helps expedite that transition

The speaker also outlines the open source nature of Vulkan (probably general knowledge but it's nice to see official reiteration of this point). That's around 43m18s. The bit about Vulkan and OpenGL being best buddies is just after that.

You could outline some of the broad points in an article if you think it's as interesting as I do. People will be interested in how the transition from OpenGL to Vulkan is seemingly paved with a yellow brick road. Vulkan was created to replace OpenGL, but it was created for the transition as well. Devs don't have to jump straight into the bath but can ease in one toe at a time.
